newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market bid $65- private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market bid $65- private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were quiet, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $65.00 per cwt and being passed by cattle owwners who have dropped asking levels to $66.00, instances $67.00, steady with last week's sales, from $67.00-$68.00 on Monday.

Snow fell overnight in central and western Texas, missing the main cattle feeding areas of the Panhandle, said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather. Most of the precipitation fell as rain and ice south and east to Dallas.
About an inch of snow registered on weather maps in the Lubbock area, Solberg said.
Precipitation for the rest of the week was seen remaining in the southern part of the state in light amounts, but a cold front remained in forecasts for all of the Plains by the weekend, he said.

Nighttime low temperatures could drop below zero Fahrenheit in Kansas and to the single digits for the Panhandle, with wind chills for the entire area ranging from 30 to 60 below zero, Solberg said. Temperatures were seen moderating by next Tuesday or Wednesday, he said.
